questions.question: How can you best tell if a trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.
questions.explanation: The easiest way to notice a trailer skid is to watch it in your mirrors. This also lets you spot skidding as early as possible.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure is lost in the emergency line?
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve protects the tractor's brakes if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. When air pressure in the emergency line is lost, the valve closes and the trailer's emergency brakes activate.

questions.question: What should you test by putting the trailer air supply control in the "emergency" position?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before starting your trip. After making sure the trailer rolls freely, pull out the trailer air supply control to the "emergency" position. Drive forward slightly and confirm the trailer does not move.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor attached to two trailers.

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor operating without a semi-trailer. Drivers must take extra care when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor's brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that helps the battery recharge.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor's brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.
questions.explanation: On combination vehicles with air brakes, the tractor protection valve protects the tractor's brakes. It keeps air in the system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak.

questions.question: Why is proper coupling technique important?

options.text: It is the same on all vehicles.
It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
It means the fifth wheel plate should not be greased.
It can be learned over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
questions.explanation: Knowing how to properly couple and uncouple combination vehicles is critical for safety. Improper coupling can be very dangerous.

questions.question: What traction does an empty combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: Empty combination vehicles stop more slowly than loaded ones. With less weight, the stiff suspension springs and strong brakes provide lower traction than they would with a full load.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the vehicle in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers occur when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo low to the ground and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: When is a trailer most likely to swing around?

options.text: When traveling in a straight line.

questions.explanation: Empty trailers need a longer stopping distance than loaded trailers. An empty or lightly loaded trailer is most likely to swing out and hit other vehicles.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the "trolley valve" or "Johnson bar") controls the trailer brakes and should only be used to test them. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: When coupling, what should you do?

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands together.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hands together.
questions.explanation: When coupling air brake hoses, connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines: one for service and one for emergencies.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: Before backing your tractor under the trailer while coupling, lock the trailer brakes. This is an important safety step.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, what should you do?

options.text: Push the accelerator to the floor.

questions.explanation: To prevent tipping, steer gently and smoothly. Avoid sudden movements when driving with a trailer.

questions.question: Pulling out the trailer air supply control tests:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you drive. Pull out the trailer air supply control to put it in the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly and make sure the trailer does not move.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Get out and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, get out immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency authorities.

questions.question: In a double or triple, which trailer should be right behind the cab?
questions.explanation: Put the most heavily-loaded trailer closest to the tractor. Put the lightest trailer in the back.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle turns a corner, what happens?

options.text: The turn should be as tight as possible.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
The rear wheels should go over the curb.
It is okay to knock over street signs that are too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels when turning. This is called off-tracking. It is more pronounced with trailers.

questions.question: When should you look into the back of the fifth wheel?

options.text: If your vehicle begins to skid.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin.

questions.question: When coupling, what is important?

options.text: You can assume all vehicles are the same.
Cracks in the mounting are acceptable.

questions.explanation: Wrong coupling and uncoupling can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Which shut-off valves should be open during a trip?

options.text: All shut-off valves except the rear ones.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves except the rear ones.
questions.explanation: Open all shut-off valves except the ones on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches the brakes on all trailers and does not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: Keeping cargo centered on a rig can:
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loads increase rollover risk. Keep the load centered on the rig to help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles, the trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: If unsure whether a trailer has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the brakes.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the brakes.
questions.explanation: Look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes to check if ABS is present.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, turn the steering wheel:

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to move.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
To the left until backing is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the steering wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ driving a single vehicle.

options.text: is safer in bad weather than

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more driving skill than single vehicles because they are longer and heavier.

questions.question: After coupling, there should be ____ between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, a driver should:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a combination vehicle turns too quickly. Keep the vehicle's center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: Having anti-lock brakes on only one axle:

options.text: will not make a difference in braking.
will provide more control when braking.
will likely cause the air brakes to malfunction.

questions.correctAnswerText: will provide more control when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes on one axle give the driver more braking control than having no anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, it is especially important that you:

options.text: Make sure there is a large enough gap for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you into their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is a large enough gap for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. Make sure there is a large enough gap in traffic to enter or cross safely.
